title: Lock and unlock
instruction: Fill in the missing words. Feel free to use paper for shifting the letters.
debrief: A cipher locks a message with a key. A weak cipher with only a few keys can be cracked by trying them; a good one can't. Https encrypts the route to a website, end-to-end encryption a message from phone to phone.

items.text: The Caesar cipher with key 3 shifts each letter three places on. CAT becomes {0}.
items.why: C → F, A → D, T → W.

items.text: Someone encrypted the message GRJ with key 3. You decrypt it by shifting three places {0}, and you get {1}.
items.why: G → D, R → O, J → G. Anyone who knows the key shifts the letters back.

items.text: Caesar has only {0} useful keys. Someone who doesn't know the key tries them one after another and {1}.

options: cracks the cipher in a few minutes

items.why: A shift of 26 letters gives back the original alphabet, so there are 25 useful keys. You can try those even by hand.

items.text: The ciphers in your phone have so many keys that {0} could try them all. That's why scammers attack {1}.
items.why: You can't break a good cipher by guessing. It's easier to get the password or the code out of a person.

items.text: The padlock and https encrypt {0}. They don't say the website is {1}.

options: the route between you and the website
the whole server and all its data

items.why: Scam websites have a padlock too. It only makes sure nobody reads the message on the way.

items.text: With end-to-end encryption only {0} have the key. The server {1}.

options: just passes the message on, unread
reads the message and stores it
corrects the message and sends it on

items.why: Only the recipient's phone unlocks the message. But whoever holds that phone can read it too.
